rationale: I shot the wide frame at seed 42 before planning it, and the picture says one thing the prose has never said: THE ROOFLINE IS A STRAIGHT LINE. eaveFor() is a region function with seven bands, so every house in a terrace shares an eave and the skyline runs flat from the courtyard's west wall to the plaza — a horizontal edge across two thirds of the frame, broken only by the church (7.8) and the clock tower (6.3), both at the extremes. c174 has been calling the top of the frame 'empty sky' for three passes and I have declined it twice on the grounds that the sky has nothing to gain; the picture says the fault was never the sky's tenants, it is that the town presents a flat silhouette to it. That is a spatial fault, it is the first thing a visitor sees, and it is rung 4b by name — which matters, because mapFlat is at 13 of 15 (developed, green, water, passages, structures, tileKinds and speciesKinds have not moved since #116) and the ladder note says every rung-4 the run has taken picked TIME. So b130 goes into buildVolumes: give the terraces HOUSES, the way NEAR_HOUSE/houseOf already does for our own block, and let them differ in height. It is the town's spine — vZ, vD, roofs, CHIMNEYS, FACES/windowLit, ROOF_FURN, the murmuration's roosts and project()'s northward lift all sit downstream — so it is a real bet and it is priced as one. The other four go to the two stalest domains and to two premises I re-priced on HEAD myself this pass rather than trusting the cue: hearthF() has exactly ONE reader in 12,000 lines (grep says line 8281, inside drawSmoke) so the rooms genuinely do not know the town is cold; puntFits' last line is `eastCloseHour() - hour > puntTripH(a) + PUNT_MIN_STAY_H`, so a 19-21h jetty arrival is refused on TIME and #128 measured 236 of 298 offers dying there; and whereN is read by exactly three lines, all of them the camera moving itself, with `followed` carrying a comment that says 'following reads, it never writes' — the observer's state is a pure sink, which is why sill x Connect is the emptiest cell in the grid.

queue.brief: `drawPuddles` is the most expensive live pass in the town — 0.94 ms of a 2.0 ms frame at peak rain — and it draws every one of the 792 pools whatever the camera is doing, so at a quarter camera most of that work lands off-frame. The cost of not culling is already measured for you (`probes/pool-cost.mjs`: drawPuddles 0.221 -> 0.308 ms, wet frame +5.5%), which is why this is a 25-minute job and not an investigation. Cull to the visible frame and give the budget back. This is a Harness brief: it changes nothing a viewer sees and does not count toward the lane's balance — the point is that b130 is about to make the roofline more expensive and there is a measured 0.9 ms sitting in a loop that mostly draws things nobody can see.
queue.successLooksLike: `perf.mjs` (or frame-cost) shows drawPuddles materially cheaper at the four quarter cameras on a wet frame, and byte-identical output: hash the canvas at pinned instants at every framing on both builds and show ZERO changed pixels. Closes c189 and c199.
queue.avoid: A cull is only free if it is exact — cull on the projected BOX with the pool's own rx/ry as margin, not on world x alone, because `project()` pinches on depth and lifts z northward, so a world-x test is not a screen test. Remember `drawPuddleLights` runs in the SCREEN pass after `applyLight` and needs the same cull or the two disagree. And carry a SIM FINGERPRINT through the before/after comparison: a `?pause`d page still runs rAF, so a canvas read is unpinned even after a synchronous draw.
